scenario: A ferry operator will load exactly seven vehicles—a hatchback, a jeep, a limousine, a minivan, a pickup, a sedan, and a van—into three holds: Forward, Midship, and Stern. Forward holds exactly two vehicles, Midship holds exactly three vehicles, and Stern holds exactly two vehicles. The loading must meet the following conditions: The jeep and the sedan are loaded into the same hold. The pickup and the van are loaded into different holds. The limousine is loaded into Midship. If the hatchback is loaded into Forward, then the pickup is loaded into Stern. Exactly one of the minivan and the van is loaded into Midship.

questions.questionStem: Which one of the following could be a complete and accurate assignment of vehicles to holds?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Forward: hatchback, pickup; Midship: jeep, limousine, sedan; Stern: minivan, van

choices.label: B
choices.text: Forward: jeep, sedan; Midship: hatchback, limousine, minivan; Stern: pickup, van

choices.label: C
choices.text: Forward: pickup, van; Midship: jeep, limousine, sedan; Stern: hatchback, minivan

choices.label: D
choices.text: Forward: jeep, sedan; Midship: hatchback, limousine, minivan; Stern: pickup, van

choices.label: E
choices.text: Forward: jeep, sedan; Midship: limousine, minivan, pickup; Stern: hatchback, van

explanations.correct: (E) respects all constraints: jeep/sedan together in Forward; pickup (Midship) and van (Stern) in different holds; limousine in Midship; exactly one of minivan/van (minivan) in Midship; group sizes 2/3/2.
explanations.A: Violates the conditional: hatchback in Forward requires pickup in Stern, but pickup is here in Forward.
explanations.B: Violates different_group: pickup and van are both in Stern.
explanations.C: Violates different_group: pickup and van are both in Forward.
explanations.D: Violates different_group: pickup and van are both in Stern.

questions.questionStem: If the jeep is loaded into Midship, then which one of the following must be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The hatchback is loaded into Forward.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The minivan is loaded into Forward.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The pickup is not loaded into Midship.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The van is loaded into Midship.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The pickup is loaded into Stern.

explanations.correct: When jeep is in Midship, so is sedan; together with limousine, Midship is full (jeep, limousine, sedan). So minivan, van, pickup, hatchback fill Forward/Stern. Since exactly one of minivan/van is in Midship—neither is—this condition fails. Re-examine: only solutions with jeep=2 are {hatchback: 3, jeep: 2, sedan: 2, limousine: 2, minivan: 1, pickup: 1, van: 2} and {hatchback: 3, jeep: 2, sedan: 2, limousine: 2, minivan: 1, pickup: 3, van: 1} and {hatchback: 1, jeep: 2, sedan: 2, limousine: 2, minivan: 3, pickup: 3, van: 1}. In all three, the minivan is in Forward or Stern but never the same across worlds—recheck: minivan positions are 1, 1, 3. So minivan is not forced to Forward. Actually the invariant across these solutions: pickup is never in Midship. So (C) must be true.
explanations.A: Hatchback could be Forward (pos 1) or Stern (pos 3); not forced.
explanations.B: Minivan could be Forward or Stern; not forced.
explanations.C: In every solution with jeep in Midship, Midship already contains jeep, limousine, and sedan, so pickup cannot be in Midship.
explanations.D: Van is not in Midship in any of these solutions.
explanations.E: Pickup could be in Forward or Stern; not forced.

questions.questionStem: Which one of the following could be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The hatchback and the pickup are both loaded into Forward.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The jeep and the van are loaded into the same hold.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The minivan and the van are both loaded into Midship.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The pickup is loaded into Midship and the hatchback is loaded into Forward.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The hatchback and the minivan are both loaded into Stern.

explanations.correct: (B) is realized in the solution {hatchback: 2, jeep: 3, sedan: 3, limousine: 2, minivan: 1, pickup: 1, van: 3}—jeep and van both in Stern.
explanations.A: If hatchback is in Forward, the conditional forces pickup into Stern, so they cannot both be in Forward.
explanations.C: Violates 'exactly one of minivan and van in Midship.'
explanations.D: If hatchback is in Forward, pickup must be in Stern, not Midship.
explanations.E: Stern holds only 2 vehicles; with hatchback and minivan in Stern, jeep/sedan must share a different hold, and then van must pair with pickup in different holds—checking enumeration, no verified solution has both hatchback=3 and minivan=3.

questions.questionStem: Which one of the following CANNOT be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The jeep is loaded into Forward.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The hatchback is loaded into Stern.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The pickup and the minivan are both loaded into Forward.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The van is loaded into Midship and the hatchback is loaded into Forward.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The minivan is loaded into Midship.

explanations.correct: (D) If hatchback is in Forward, the conditional forces pickup into Stern. Then van must be in a different hold from pickup, so van is Forward or Midship. If van is in Midship, then minivan is not (exactly one of them in Midship ✓). Midship then contains limousine and van plus one more. Forward contains hatchback and one other. jeep/sedan must pair, so they go together into Midship or Stern. Stern already has pickup; the second Stern slot must be jeep or sedan or minivan. But jeep and sedan must be together, so both into Midship (full with limousine, van, jeep+sedan = 4, too many) or both into Stern (with pickup = 3, too many). Contradiction—no valid world.
explanations.C: Realized in e.g. {hatchback: 2, jeep: 3, sedan: 3, minivan: 1, pickup: 1, van: 2}.
explanations.E: Realized in several solutions where minivan is in Midship.

questions.questionStem: If the pickup is loaded into Forward, then which one of the following must be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The hatchback is loaded into Midship.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The jeep is loaded into Stern.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The van is not loaded into Midship.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The sedan is loaded into Midship.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The minivan is loaded into Forward.

explanations.correct: If pickup is in Forward, then hatchback is not in Forward (else pickup would be in Stern). Checking enumerated solutions with pickup=1: {hatchback: 2, jeep: 3, sedan: 3, limousine: 2, minivan: 1, pickup: 1, van: 2} and {hatchback: 3, jeep: 2, sedan: 2, limousine: 2, minivan: 1, pickup: 1, van: 2} and {hatchback: 2, jeep: 3, sedan: 3, limousine: 2, minivan: 1, pickup: 1, van: 2}. Hatchback is in Midship or Stern; not forced to Midship. Reviewing: jeep is 3 or 2—not forced. Van is always 2 (Midship)—so (C) is false. The invariant is that the van is in Midship in every such solution, so 'van is NOT in Midship' must be FALSE; therefore the must-be-true answer is actually the negation. Correct inference: the van must be in Midship.
explanations.A: Hatchback could be in Midship or Stern.
explanations.B: Jeep could be in Midship or Stern.
explanations.C: In every solution with pickup in Forward, van is in Midship—so this is false.
explanations.D: Sedan could be in Midship or Stern.
explanations.E: Minivan is in Forward in all such solutions—this actually must be true.
